scope: source-scoped actual-width qualification, four bounded full-BPTT continuation witnesses and two BF16 backward-owner diagnostics
interpretation_notes: Original records and original initial failures are unchanged; job success is not numerical qualification.
BF16 is autocast projection arithmetic with FP32 masters, gradients, moments and scalar/SSD state; no whole-model BF16 storage claim.

highest_scaled_error_witnesses retains up to three of the raw records eight largest scaled-error tensor witnesses, not a guaranteed global absolute-error maximum; nested max_abs fields are full-tree maxima.
Long failure arrays are reduced to counts and bounded examples; original file hashes identify the complete records.
Qualification continuation detaches private state between updates; whole/chunk diagnostics retain full BPTT without optimizer or state detach.
CPU continuation v9 has valid completed FP32/BF16 records, but its outer job failed when the later FP64 metadata policy rejected fp64; fixed-source FP64 v10 is a distinct run.
All BF16 whole/chunk witnesses retain zero support, logical metadata and gradient-connectivity differences; finite value/state deviations remain.
Same-owner FC-S variability means a restore-only explanation is not supported; the diagnostic does not isolate a backend kernel or promise determinism.
Scalar FP64 AdamW predictions use the actual stored scalar input gradients/moments; agreement explains selected update differences, not training quality.
No threshold relaxation, extra shape sweep, or relabeling of earlier failures is applied.
